canonicalEncoding.objects: Plain data only; keys sorted by UTF-16 code units; no getters, symbols or toJSON hooks.
canonicalEncoding.arrays: Dense ordered arrays without extra properties.
canonicalEncoding.scalars: null, booleans, strings with JSON escaping and safe integers except negative zero.
canonicalEncoding.bounds: Depth, node count and output byte count are bounded; cycles and unsupported values reject.

artifactIdentity: SHA-256 of exact canonical or target bytes, with explicit domain, schema, contract and byte length. The artifact key hashes the full descriptor, preserving domain separation.
semanticFingerprint: Exact artifact identity is the conservative default. Ignoring byte differences requires a separate reuse contract and evidence.
actionIdentity: Canonical pass-definition identity, ordered input artifacts, explicit parameters, semantic identity, resource policy and dependencies. Records with incomplete implementation closure are not sufficient for untrusted cache reuse.
verification: Re-hash execution, definition, implementation, action, dependencies and every input/output artifact.
Recompute ActionId; validate input/output contracts, assumption policy and exact fingerprint provenance.
Resolve evidence bytes and invoke caller-configured independent checkers against the exact relation, action, input, output and assumption subject.
A missing required evidence kind or unavailable checker fails closed.
Integrity verification is not preservation verification; serialized records never mint kernel authority.
currentBuildCoverage: source preparation and kernel checking as an observed composite edge
checked admissions to TypeScript as an observed composite edge
TypeScript to JavaScript, declarations and source map with the actual flags and output basename
remaining: canonical artifacts for individual internal IR stages
complete generated compiler/runtime and TypeScript package closure
archive resolution of all referenced source and implementation bytes
portableDigestRule: A portable record supplied with artifact labels remains requiresByteVerification. Legacy specialization records remain unbound. Neither implies byte verification or a proof.
